title: Desk Guidance: Project Records per Owner and per Building
content:
# Desk Guidance — Project Records per Owner and per Building

The rule the desk applies when a new Equipment Replacement & Retrofit Projects estimate is opened for an owner who already holds projects.

## Rule

A building owner may carry as many projects as they have buildings and scopes; there is no upper count of projects per owner. Several projects may run at one building at the same time where their scopes do not overlap. A second project is not opened for a scope already covered by a project in estimated, awarded, scheduled or in progress status at the same building; the existing project's scope is changed instead through a change order. Projects in closed, cancelled or declined status never block a new estimate.

Each project holds its own contract value, its own retainage and its own change allowance. Nothing is pooled between projects, so a credit on one project is never set against the balance of another.

## What decides whether a scope is already covered

The office's project records decide it, read before the new estimate is opened: the building, the scope class and the status of each project standing there. A project counts as live for this purpose in exactly four statuses — estimated, awarded, scheduled and in progress. The class the existing project was written at and the day it was estimated do not matter; the same building and the same scope class are what make it the same scope.

## Judgement table

| Existing project at the same building | Same scope class | Result for the new estimate |
|---|---|---|
| estimated, awarded, scheduled or in progress | yes | not opened; the existing project's scope is changed by change order |
| estimated, awarded, scheduled or in progress | no (a different scope) | opened; two projects may run at one building |
| closed, cancelled or declined | yes or no | opened; a finished or stopped project never blocks |
| none | — | opened |

## Points of judgement

**An owner has four buildings and asks for a fifth project at a building where two projects already run.** The count of projects is never the limit; the only question is whether the fifth scope overlaps a live scope at that building.

**A chiller replacement was estimated last month at a building and the owner now asks for a second chiller replacement estimate there.** The first project is in estimated status and covers that scope; the second is not opened, and the first project's scope is changed through a change order instead.

**A project at the building was cancelled last year for the same scope.** A cancelled project never blocks; the new estimate is opened.
